title: Factorization through a relative curve
statement: Let $S$ be either the spectrum of a field or an excellent integral trait [def-exc-excellent-ring, def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], with generic point $s$, and let $X\to S$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], dominant, finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with $X$ integral [def-pc-integral-scheme]. If the generic fibre $X_s$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] has dimension $d\geq1$ [def-kun-dimension], then there are an excellent integral scheme $Y$ [def-exc-excellent-ring, def-pc-integral-scheme], a projective [def-kun-projective] dominant finite-type morphism $Y\to S$ whose generic fibre $Y_s$ has dimension $d-1$, an excellent integral scheme $X_0$, a proper dominant generically finite morphism $a:X_0\to X$ (finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] over a dense open of $X$), and a proper dominant morphism $g:X_0\to Y$ such that the composites $X_0\xrightarrow{a}X\to S$ and $X_0\xrightarrow{g}Y\to S$ are equal, and such that the extension of function fields $\kappa(Y)\subset\kappa(X_0)$ [def-sc-function-field] induced by $g$ has transcendence degree one [def-kun-transcendence-degree]. Excellence of a scheme means excellence of its affine coordinate rings.

source.place: Expose X, proof of Theorem 3.5, Step 5, printed p. 163: choose a rational map h' with relative transcendence degree one and take the schematic image after a projective modification.
